_comment: Tier-2 for dune::hyperelasticity#0, #1 and #4, on an 8x8 dimRange=2 Neo-Hookean problem; wall time 56 s warm on 2026-08-06 (dune-fem 2.12.0.2). #0 and #1 are checked by INTEGRATING the energy density at the reference configuration, which needs no solve: the correct W = mu/2 (tr C - d) - mu ln J + lam/2 (ln J)^2 integrates to 0 at F = I, while dropping the -d leaves exactly mu/2*d; and det(grad(u)) at the reference is 0.000000e+00, so ln(J) is -inf — F = grad(u) really is singular there. #4 IS FALSIFIED AS WRITTEN and the fixture asserts the correction. The claim says to specify just the energy W and let scheme.solve() build the derivatives. Measured, dune-fem accepts neither energy route: derivative(Pi, uh, v) is a ONE-form and galerkin rejects it with ValueError 'Integrands model requires form with at least two arguments.', and taking P = dW/dF with ufl.variable + ufl.diff dies in dune's own code generator with TypeError 'RestrictionPropagator.variable() takes 3 positional arguments but 4 were given'. The first variation has to be written out (here P = mu(F - F^-T) + lam ln(J) F^-T); what IS automatic is the TANGENT, and the fixture shows that by solving with 3 Newton iterations and no hand-coded Jacobian. hyperelasticity#2 (load stepping) is NOT covered: at the load reachable here the one-shot solve converged in the same 3 Newton iterations as each of ten substeps, so the configuration does not distinguish them and claiming it would be false coverage.
expect_in_output: Integrands model requires form with at least two arguments.
